A bicycle gear system works by changing the relationship between the chainring in the front and the sprocket in the rear, which adjusts how far the chain pulls the bike forward for each pedal revolution.

The main components are the chainring attached to the crank, the rear cassette mounted on the wheel hub, and the chain connecting them. When you pedal, the chainring turns the chain. The chain then pulls on one of the rear sprockets, turning the wheel. The bike moves forward because the rear wheel is forced to rotate by this action.
